payload.title: Why your scheduled job fails silently on macOS
payload.question: why does my launchd job hang with no error and no output
payload.symptom: A background job that should text or push finishes with no error, sends nothing, and its own health check still reports green.
payload.cause: Under launchd, osascript driving Messages blocks on a TCC Automation prompt that a background context cannot display. Nothing resolves it, so it hangs until timeout.
payload.measured: 90 second timeout, no error returned, no message sent.
payload.fix: Run anything that pushes or sends as a launchd agent in a user session with Automation granted, and split sending into a queue step that never blocks and a drain step that only runs where permission exists.
payload.why_it_matters: The failure is not the hang. Silence looks identical to nothing happened, so a watchdog wired to text you goes quiet overnight while reporting itself healthy.

payload.title: When an API call half succeeds and you read it as failed
payload.question: api call returned an error but some writes went through
payload.symptom: A command performs several writes, one is rejected, and the error message makes it look as though nothing happened.
payload.cause: Multi-write operations are rarely atomic. A DNS change that sets an A record and a CNAME can have the A record rejected as invalid while the CNAME write succeeds.
payload.measured: HTTP 422 on one record, HTTP 200 on the other. Reading 'failed' and moving on left the domain half-changed and took it down.
payload.fix: After any command that reports partial failure, read the resulting state back rather than trusting the error. Verify what IS, never what you think you did.
payload.why_it_matters: Half-succeeded operations leave systems in states no one designed, and the error message is actively misleading about it.

payload.title: Never replace a live page before checking what it captures
payload.question: redesigned landing page and lost signups
payload.symptom: A better looking page ships and enquiries quietly stop.
payload.cause: The old page was doing something invisible in the markup — a form wired to a vendor inbox, a chat widget, a tracking hook — and the replacement did not carry it.
payload.measured: A form endpoint present on the old builder page was absent from the replacement. Every visitor in that window hit a dead form and left no trace.
payload.fix: Before migrating any customer-facing surface, enumerate what it captures, sends and receives, and prove the replacement does the same BEFORE cutover.
payload.why_it_matters: A prettier page that captures nothing is strictly worse than an ugly one that captures, and the loss is invisible because non-events are not logged.

payload.title: Why a partial view is more dangerous than no view
payload.question: script sees only some files and reports success
payload.symptom: A scan or sync reports clean results that are quietly wrong.
payload.cause: Recent macOS blocks scheduled jobs from protected directories, and the block presents as absence rather than as a permission error. Code that sees half a directory concludes the other half does not exist.
payload.measured: A convergence loop declared success against a filesystem it could only partly read.
payload.fix: Make jobs assert what they could not read, and refuse to conclude when the evidence is incomplete. Report degraded rather than clean.
payload.why_it_matters: No answer is recoverable. A confident wrong answer propagates into everything downstream that trusted it.

payload.title: Exit code zero is not delivery
payload.question: osascript returned 0 but the message never arrived
payload.symptom: A send command succeeds and the recipient receives nothing.
payload.cause: The sending tool reports that it raised no error, which is a different claim from the message being delivered. The tool that queues is not the system that delivers.
payload.measured: osascript exited 0 against an unroutable handle with nothing delivered.
payload.fix: Verify against the store that records delivery — poll the messages database for the row — rather than trusting the caller's exit status.
payload.why_it_matters: Every notification path built on exit codes is silently unreliable, and it fails exactly when you most need to hear from it.

payload.what_this_is: The public view of one business's digital twin. An agent can read what this business is, what it offers, and act on it directly — the website is a projection of this surface, not the other way round.

lessons.what: operational knowledge this twin has published, as rapp/1 frames

offers.what: Priority access when the product fully launches. Boxes ship in join order; the first group is set up directly.

fields.name: string, required
fields.note: string, optional — what the business would want handled
fields.source: string, optional — set to your agent name

offers.consent: Only submit on behalf of a human who asked you to. This is a real business waitlist and every entry is read by a person.

capabilities_you_may_use: read this document and any stream it lists
quote a lesson, citing its frame_hash
join the waitlist on an explicit human request
federate: mint your own stream and reference these hashes
payload.privacy: Every frame on the public streams passes a deny-by-default gate: a field allowlist, shape scans for emails, phones, personal paths, IPs, tokens, addresses and account identifiers, plus a scan against real held secrets. Nothing about a customer is ever published.

federation.pattern: one stream, one writer — others federate as equal streams
